question.text: Exit load on an equity MF is typically:

explanation.text: The Logic: Exit loads on equity mutual funds are designed to discourage short-term redemptions that disrupt portfolio management. A common industry convention for diversified equity schemes is an exit load of about 1% on units redeemed within 365 days of purchase, with no exit load thereafter; the exact figure is disclosed in each scheme's offer document and factsheet. The Trap: "Always zero" ignores that most equity schemes do levy a short-holding-period load; 10% and 50% are far above typical regulatory and industry norms for open-ended equity MFs. Note: The Portfolio Managers (NISM-Series-XXI-B) workbook states that mutual fund factsheets disclose loads and expenses, and discusses PMS exit-load caps (3%, 2%, 1% over the first three years), but does not specifically state a typical equity MF exit load of 1% within 365 days. That figure is offered here as general industry convention.
